goal: Broaden interview evidence across Ukrainian and international sources without duplicating semantic concepts or inflating the catalog with low-value trivia.

rules: Wording variants never create another canonical question.
Theory and scenario questions remain separate only when they test materially different skills.
A source hit normally strengthens evidence/prevalence; it does not automatically create a question.
Absence from the catalog is necessary but not sufficient: independent recurrence and interview value must justify addition.
Ukrainian and international interview sources have equal market/prevalence priority.
Official docs/specifications validate technical answers; interview banks validate recurrence and interview intent.
Freshness matters most for tools, delivery practices, mobile platforms and AI; classic testing fundamentals do not become obsolete merely because the source is older.

sources.title: DOU — 400+ QA interview questions for Junior, Middle, Senior
What questions to ask a QA engineer: a technical interviewer's perspective

findings: DOU 400+ remains valuable Ukrainian-market evidence but its 416 raw prompts include wording/concept duplicates and should never be treated as 416 unique catalog additions.
Fresh Ukrainian interviewer guidance confirms that fundamentals remain important but should be asked through explanation, examples and scenarios rather than rote definitions.
Current Ukrainian junior-market material still explicitly asks severity vs priority, test case vs checklist, bug reports, smoke/regression/sanity and SDLC/STLC.
DOU 400+ practical and Senior sections provide stronger signal than its tool/API trivia for release risk, missing documentation, prioritization, RCA and collaboration.

sources.note: Publisher states the bank is informed by hiring-manager debriefs across 40+ QA searches in the prior 18 months.

sources.role: QA/SDET-specific interview signals for Git, automation, CI/CD and mobile

findings: 2026 sources strongly confirm that classic fundamentals remain relevant, so the age of DOU 250/400 alone is not a reason to remove them.
The current market puts more weight on applied judgment: what not to test, what not to automate, flaky-test diagnosis, missing requirements, CI/CD, release risk and quality ownership.
AI-assisted and agentic testing are now visible interview topics, but GimmeJob's modern-SDET authored set already covers most of the meaningful AI decision boundaries.
Current automation sources emphasize framework selection, pipeline behavior and debugging over memorizing Selenium APIs.
Current mobile sources emphasize device strategy, network transitions/offline sync, pre-release distribution, proxy debugging, upgrade paths and mobile CI/CD.
Risk-based mobile device/OS coverage is already directly represented by emulator-simulator-real-device, so fresh device-matrix sources should merge there rather than create a new question.

Generic asynchronous/eventually-consistent systems are already covered by event-driven-contract-testing, message-ordering-replay-dead-letter and async-trace-correlation; no generic duplicate is recommended.
WebSocket testing remains a distinct gap because persistent connection lifecycle and bidirectional real-time behavior are not directly represented in the main interview catalog.
Offline mobile synchronization and app upgrade/local-data migration remain distinct mobile interview intents not adequately represented by notification/offline mentions elsewhere.
Shift-left exists as learning/tagged content but not as a directly discoverable interview question; 2026 recurrence justifies a canonical applied question.
Automation framework components are covered, but choosing between Playwright/Selenium/Cypress based on context is a separate current interview intent and remains a gap.

dou400.treatment: Keep as first-class Ukrainian prevalence/coverage evidence; map overlapping prompts to canonical questions and add only distinct high-value concepts.

globalSecondPass.method: Rechecked every proposed net-new concept against authored interview sets and repo-wide content search, then collapsed overlaps into canonical source merges.

AI human-decision boundaries -> existing AI authored questions

phase1Result.expectedCatalogGrowth: small; source diversity and prevalence evidence should change much more than question count

phase2ApplicationPlan: Add only the approved canonical questions from the candidate ledger with stable IDs, EN/UA text, practical examples and answer-authority sources.
Register selected new interview-market sources in content/interview/sources.json.
Merge source IDs into existing canonical questions where fresh sources independently reinforce the same interview intent.
Re-run prevalence review using Ukrainian and international recurrence together; do not promote specialist/tool-specific questions merely because a long bank lists them.
Run repository content validation and full verification only after production content is intentionally changed.
Use one scoped PR for the completed production application, not one PR per source or batch.
